title: Close the ~/ and $HOME/ containment bypass in both runtimes
action: SECURITY FIX-FIRST (GH #71 D8). VERIFIED HOLE, reproduce it yourself first against .bee/bin/hooks/bee-write-guard.mjs by piping a hook payload on stdin from the repo root: a Bash command redirecting to an ABSOLUTE path under the user's home denies exit 2 with the containment message, while the SAME destination written as ~/... or $HOME/... exits 0. Cause: extractBashTargets (packages/bee/lib/guards.mjs, around :1531-1741) emits the token verbatim; a leading tilde-slash is neither absolute nor contains dot-dot, so canonicalRelPath (bee-write-guard.mjs:65-114) resolves it against cwd as a literal directory named '~' or '$HOME' and yields an in-repo relative path that passes containment and flows into checkWrite. BROAD_TARGETS catches a bare '~' only (guards.mjs:1533), not '~/x'. (1) RED FIRST: add differential coverage proving all three spellings of one out-of-worktree destination get the SAME verdict — extend the existing guard suites (packages/bee/hooks/test_write_guard.mjs escapeRows around :803, packages/bee/tests/test_bee_write_guard_hook.mjs) and the Rust differential rig (crates/queen-bee/tests/writeguard_bash.rs, using assert_deny_conformant so mjs and rust stderr stay byte-identical). Run it against unmodified code and capture the RED output. (2) FIX: handle a leading tilde-slash, $HOME/ and ${HOME}/ in extracted Bash targets BEFORE containment. Choose expand-then-contain or deny-outright and justify the choice in a comment — deny is the safer default and needs no environment read, but expand keeps a legitimate in-home path checkable against a declared root later (gmr-2 depends on this choice, so state it). Whatever you choose, a bare '~' must keep today's behavior. (3) Both runtimes, byte-identical decisions and byte-identical deny strings: packages/bee/lib/guards.mjs plus crates/bee-core/src/guards.rs (and write_guard.rs if the seam lives there). (4) Vendor + regen in order: node scripts/render_plugin_skill_trees.mjs, node packages/bee/scripts/onboard_bee.mjs --repo-root . --apply, node scripts/impact_registry.mjs --write, node scripts/release_manifest.mjs --write; md5sum of each changed .bee/bin/** file must equal its packages/bee/** twin (the Rust conformance rig sha256-verifies them). (5) rust-port D1 mirror artifact: file a rust-port-tagged backlog item naming the behavior delta via the backlog CLI. (6) Verify with the FULL suite, never an impacted run.

truths: The three spellings of one out-of-worktree destination (absolute, tilde-slash, $HOME/) now receive the SAME verdict, proven by a test that was RED before the fix — capture that red output.
A bare '~' keeps today's behavior (BROAD_TARGETS, guards.mjs:1533).
The mjs and Rust hooks agree on the verdict AND on the deny string, proven through the differential harness (assert_deny_conformant).
In-repo paths are unaffected: every pre-existing guard test passes unedited.
The chosen strategy (expand vs deny) is stated in a comment with its reason, because gmr-2 builds on it.
md5sum of every changed .bee/bin/** file equals its packages/bee/** twin.
A rust-port-tagged backlog item names the behavior delta.
node scripts/run_verify.mjs (FULL) exits 0; report the summary line verbatim.
prohibitions: Do NOT weaken, edit, or skip any existing guard test to get green — they encode the wall.
Do NOT introduce a fail-open path: an error while handling the prefix must deny, never allow.
Do NOT implement gmr-2's declared-root allowlist here; this cell only closes the bypass.
Do NOT cap on an impacted run.
Do NOT change .bee/state.json phase or gates.

verify: node scripts/ledger_parity.mjs --check && node scripts/release_manifest.mjs --check && node scripts/run_verify.mjs
